subject.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata

question: When a structured approval contains a non-empty `toolCallId` that does not uniquely match an active prompt, should ACP fail closed or fall back to the sole prompt sharing its `sessionKey`?
rationale: This determines whether an explicit correlation mismatch is treated as authoritative security-boundary evidence or tolerated for backward compatibility; tests can encode either policy, but repository intent is required.

options.title: Make the identifier authoritative
options.body: Request permission only for a unique identifier match when `toolCallId` is present, while retaining session-only fallback for legacy events where it is absent.

options.title: Preserve the sole-prompt fallback
options.body: Continue routing unmatched identifiers to the only pending prompt for the session, accepting the possibility that malformed or stale metadata can bind across an identifier mismatch.

recommendation.title: Make the identifier authoritative
recommendation.body: Request permission only for a unique identifier match when `toolCallId` is present, while retaining session-only fallback for legacy events where it is absent.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP exec approval relay and its existing session-correlation behavior.
